/-!
# Erdős Problem 362

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/362](https://www.erdosproblems.com/362)
- [Er65] Erdős, P., *Extremal problems in number theory*. Proc. Sympos. Pure Math., Vol. VIII
  (1965), 181-189.
- [Er73] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of
  combinatorial theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971)
  (1973), 117-138.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [SaSz65] Sárközi, A. and Szemerédi, E., *Über ein Problem von Erdős und Moser*. Acta Arith.
  (1965), 205-208.
- [St80] Stanley, Richard P., *Weyl groups, the hard Lefschetz theorem, and the Sperner property*.

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos362

/--
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be a finite set of size $N$. Is it true that, for any fixed $t$,
there are
$$\ll \frac{2^N}{N^{3/2}}$$
many $S\subseteq A$ such that $\sum_{n\in S}n=t$?

Erdős and Moser [Er65] proved the first bound with an additional factor of $(\log n)^{3/2}$.
This was removed by Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz65], thereby answering the first question in the
affirmative. Stanley [St80] has shown that this quantity is maximised when
$A=\{-\lfloor \frac{N-1}{2}\rfloor,\ldots,\lfloor\frac{N}{2}\rfloor\}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos362.lean#L2541"]
theorem erdos_362 : answer(True) ↔ ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (A : Finset ℕ) (t : ℕ), A.Nonempty →
    ({S ∈ A.powerset | ∑ n ∈ S, n = t}.card : ℝ) ≤ C * 2 ^ A.card / (A.card : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
If we further ask that $\lvert S\rvert=l$ (for any fixed $l$) then is the number of solutions
$$\ll \frac{2^N}{N^2},$$
with the implied constant independent of $l$ and $t$?

The second question was answered in the affirmative by Halász [Ha77], as a consequence of a more
general multi-dimensional result.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos362.lean#L2541"]
theorem erdos_362.variants.fixed_card : answer(True) ↔ ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (A : Finset ℕ) (l t : ℕ),
    A.Nonempty →
      ({S ∈ A.powersetCard l | ∑ n ∈ S, n = t}.card : ℝ) ≤ C * 2 ^ A.card / (A.card : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos362

reformulations.difference: Erdős's original formulation in [Er65] allows arbitrary distinct real numbers; Lean uses a finite set of natural numbers and a natural-number target.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The real-number bound immediately implies the natural-number bound. Conversely, a finite positive-real subset-sum fibre can be modeled by distinct positive integers: its equal-sum equations have rational coefficients, so choose a rational solution sufficiently close to the original positive, distinct entries and clear denominators. All members of the original fibre remain in one fibre. For an arbitrary real set of size N ≥ 2, select m ≥ N/3 nonzero entries of the same sign and condition on the other entries. Apply the positive-real bound, negating the selected entries if necessary. Summing over the other choices gives C·2^N/m^(3/2) ≤ 3^(3/2)C·2^N/N^(3/2). The N = 1 case is absorbed into the constant. Thus existence of an absolute uniform constant is equivalent.

reformulations.difference: The original fixed-cardinality question in [Er65]/[Er73] concerns distinct real numbers, whereas Lean quantifies over finite sets of natural numbers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The real-number statement implies the natural-number statement directly. For the converse, translate any finite real set far enough to make all its entries positive. For l-element subsets this shifts every sum by the same amount l times the translation, preserving the fibre size. Model that positive-real fibre by distinct positive rationals satisfying its rational linear equal-sum equations, then clear denominators. This preserves the set's size, the prescribed subset cardinality, and at least all members of the original fibre. The uniform natural-number bound therefore bounds every real-number fibre with the same constant.

review.notes: Both declarations have the correct exponents, uniform quantifier order, counting predicates, and affirmative answers. Lean experiments checked empty and singleton inputs, inclusion of 0, l = 0, and l > A.card. The nonempty hypothesis prevents zero denominators; positivity of C follows from the bounds themselves. The exact linked external proof and both dependencies compiled successfully, and its theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Its sqrt(N)^3 denominator was proved equivalent to N^(3/2) in scratch Lean. The current public Erdős database records problem 362 as proved (Lean), agreeing with the metadata. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/362 was blocked by Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers; comparisons used the cited primary papers instead. Halász's full text was unavailable, so its historical attribution was not independently checked from that paper.
